real_conflicts: Proposal to 'shift the performer list to the left side' (Composition Verdict) directly conflicts with the mandate for expressive typography. Stacking the performer names (Nia Cole, Static Bloom, Armand Vale) into a single column with the date and venue creates a dense, static block of text. This 'tidy' arrangement neutralizes the visual energy of the poster and fails to reflect the 'improvisation' and 'syncopation' required by the brief. It treats the text as a data table rather than a visual element.

Proposal to 'replace the smooth blue curve with a distorted, glitched... effect' (Visual Concept Verdict) risks harming the typographic hierarchy. If the background imagery becomes too chaotic or 'glitched,' it will compete with the headline for attention. The headline needs a relatively stable visual anchor to be legible; if the background is too aggressive, the text becomes a mere label rather than an integrated part of the composition.
accepted: Proposal to 'break the symmetry' (Composition Verdict). The current rigid centering of the headline and the bisecting vertical line are detrimental to the 'experimental' voice. The text must be liberated from the grid to convey 'tension.'

Proposal to 'apply a subtle noise/grain texture overlay' (Color Verdict). This supports the typographic mandate by giving the text a tactile, analog quality, moving it away from the sterile 'digital overlay' look of the current neon glow.
concession: I concede that the headline font does not need to be 'distorted' or 'glitched' (as per my original revision). A heavy, geometric sans-serif can work if it is manipulated spatially. The 'distortion' should be achieved through the layout and interaction with the graphics, not by warping the letterforms themselves, which risks illegibility.
compromise: Instead of shifting the text to a single column, we will break the symmetry by applying a horizontal shear (skew) to the entire headline stack ('BLUE HOUR / RED NOISE') to introduce kinetic energy. We will then allow the red 'noise' waveform to physically intersect and 'cut' through the letters of 'RED NOISE' (creating a depth effect), while the performer names remain on the right but are set in a smaller, monospaced typeface to contrast with the headline, reinforcing the 'static' aesthetic without creating a dense block.
nonnegotiable: The headline 'BLUE HOUR / RED NOISE' must not sit statically on top of the graphics. It must interact with the waveform (via intersection, masking, or depth) to function as an expressive visual material rather than a decorative label.
